subject: Banking
title: Insider Trading Scandals
description: A short lesson to help you apply Insider Trading Scandals.

hook.text: Raj Rajaratnam made $63 million trading on tips from Goldman Sachs board member Rajat Gupta. Both went to prison.

buildup.text: Insider trading means buying or selling stocks based on confidential information not available to the public.

discovery.text: Investment bankers know about deals before they are announced.

twist.text: The SEC uses phone taps, email surveillance, and pattern analysis to catch traders.

climax.text: Markets work only if outsiders trust the price; insider trading turns privileged access into the edge.

punchline.text: $63 million from insider tips. Both the trader and the tipper went to prison.

quiz.question: What is insider trading?
options: Buying or selling stocks based on confidential non-public information

details.summary: Insider trading occurs when individuals trade securities based on material non-public information, such as upcoming mergers or earnings results, giving them an illegal advantage over regular investors.
details.whyItMatters: Insider trading scandals erode public trust in financial markets. If insiders consistently profit from secret information, ordinary investors lose confidence that markets are fair, undermining the entire capital allocation system.
takeaways: Material non-public information cannot legally be used for trading
The SEC uses data analytics to detect suspicious trading patterns
Raj Rajaratnam and Ivan Boesky are among the most famous insider traders

faq.question: How does the SEC catch insider traders?
faq.answer: The SEC uses sophisticated data analytics to identify unusual trading patterns before major announcements. Phone records, email surveillance, and tips from informants also play key roles. Pattern recognition has become increasingly automated.

faq.question: What are the penalties for insider trading?
faq.answer: Federal law allows fines up to three times the profit gained and imprisonment up to 20 years. In practice, sentences vary widely. Raj Rajaratnam received 11 years, while many receive shorter sentences or only pay fines.
